title: Time-proportional SLA crediting for partial dedicated-pool degradations
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Problem: Our current SLA crediting model for Dedicated pools treats outages as coarse-grained events (e.g., full-pool downtime or minute-level binary availability). This fails to compensate customers when a pool is partially degraded: reduced throughput due to noisy neighbors, kernel regressions, or transient autoscaler under-provisioning. Customers with reserved throughput should receive time-proportional credits when delivered throughput falls below their committed level, including during partial-capacity windows and cross-region failovers.

Scope: Implement time-proportional SLA credits that compute the shortfall as the difference between committed reserved throughput and observed delivered throughput aggregated per tenant across each dedicated pool, normalized by scheduled reservation intervals. Integrate with existing billing pipeline so credits appear on monthly invoices and are automatically applied or flagged for finance review if above a threshold. This ticket focuses on the metering, calculation, and automatic-credit wiring; UI work (console display) is a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Credit formula defined and reviewed: per-tenant credit = price_per_unit * sum_over_windows(max(0, committed_tpu - delivered_tpu_window) * window_duration_fraction)
Metering pipeline emits per-tenant per-window delivered_tpu samples with stable semantics (60s windows) and latency <= 2 minutes to billing ingestion
Billing pipeline computes credits automatically and posts ledger entries with traceable meters and raw samples
Automated tests and end-to-end canary produce expected credits for three synthetic scenarios (full outage, 50% throughput for 10 minutes, gradual decline then recovery)
Backfill job can recompute credits for the last 30 days and reconciles with finance CSVs within 0.1% precision for sample customers
No user-visible increase in request path P95 latency and metering ingestion cost within budget (see metrics below)
implementation_plan: Design: finalize credit formula & edge cases (throttles, client-side retries, multi-region double-counting) — design doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/dedicated-sla-proportional (internal)
Metering: extend dedicated-metrics emitter to publish 'delivered_tpu' and 'requested_tpu' at 60s granularity per tenant/pool; include pool_id, tenant_id, region, window_start_iso
Storage: create time-series partition 'billing.dedicated_window_samples' (schema documented in Confluence) to store 60s samples for 90-day retention
Computation: implement billing job 'compute_time_proportional_sla' that consumes window samples and committed reservations, applies window-level shortfall calc, aggregates to invoice-period credits
Idempotency: ensure job is idempotent and supports window-level upserts; include an 'origin' tag for samples (runtime-emitter vs backfill) to avoid double-counts

Edge handling: define treatment for transient spikes (smoothing via 3-sample moving median) and for windows with incomplete data (apply conservative delivered_tpu = min(observed, committed) and mark for manual review if > 5% of windows missing),

Integration: wire computed credits to billing-ledger with comment keys linking back to sample IDs and PRs; include support for automatic invoice crediting and finance notification when monthly credit > $5k
Backfill: implement streaming backfill that can recompute for last 30 days using historical samples or approximate using aggregated per-minute logs if raw samples are missing

Observability: add dashboards: 'dedicated:delivered_vs_committed', 'billing:credits_by_customer', and tracing for compute job; instrument alert when delivered/committed delta > 20% across any pool for > 5 minutes
metrics: Correctness: computed credit amount matches naive ground-truth simulation within 0.5% for synthetic workloads
Latency: metering sample to billing ingestion end-to-end < 2 minutes (target)
Cost: incremental storage < 15% of current billing DB spend; compute job run time < 45 minutes for full 30-day backfill on standard cluster
Reliability: compute job idempotent and supports retry with at-most-once ledger writes (replay-safe)
Adoption: initial rollout to 10 pilot customers (reserved pools) and observe expected credits for at least 2 incident scenarios
testing_plan: Unit tests for sample aggregation, credit math, and window edge-cases
Integration test wiring meter -> store -> compute -> ledger using test harness with synthetic samples
Chaos test: inject degraded delivered_tpu on a canary pool (simulate noisy neighbor) and validate credits computed and posted within SLA
Regression test: ensure existing 'full-pool outage' credit paths still produce identical outputs when degradation is binary
Manual finance reconciliation: generate CSVs for pilot customers and compare to seed naive calc in spreadsheet
Performance test: run backfill on staging dataset sized like prod 30-day to validate timing and memory
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature flag off — deploy metering emitter and storage schema changes to staging
Stage 1: Enable emitter for small internal pilot orgs (5 customers) for 7 days; validate samples and dashboards
Stage 2: Turn on compute job in dry-run mode for 2 production customers (no automated credits; ledger entries as draft) for 14 days
Stage 3: Review finance and support feedback; enable automatic invoice credits for pilot customers via feature flag
Stage 4: Gradual increase to 10-20% of dedicated customers over 4 weeks, then GA for all Dedicated tenants
Abort plan: if credit computation diverges >2% from expected or compute costs exceed threshold, roll back compute job and revert emitter changes
migration_steps: Run backfill job to compute credits for last 30 days; store results as 'backfill_v1' origin tag
Coordinate with Finance on ledger ingestion format and reconciliation cadence; deliver sample CSV and mapping document
For tenants with overlapping legacy credits, create mapping table to prevent double crediting and retire legacy path after verification
Communicate to customers via Console message and e-mail about new time-proportional credits and how they will appear on invoices
Schedule finance runbook for manual approvals if monthly auto-credit exceeds configured threshold
open_questions: Q1: How should we treat client-side retries that increase requested_tpu but do not increase delivered_tpu? (proposal: ignore requested_tpu for credit calc; use only delivered_tpu and router-acknowledge counts)
Q2: Should credits be calculated in USD at time-of-window or using invoice-period FX conversion? (proposal: calculate credits in invoice currency using rate at invoice time — needs finance signoff)
Q3: What threshold of missing windows triggers manual review? Proposed 5% of windows per invoice period

Q4: How to avoid double-credit when customer has both Dedicated reservation and transient Hosted fallbacks? (proposal: attribute samples by tenancy and pool; if multiple pools serve same tenant, apply max-delivered across pools after de-dup logic)

Q5: Should extremely short degradations (<= 2 windows / 2 minutes) be ignored to prevent noise credits? (proposal: apply 3-sample smoothing; still bill any nonzero shortfall but mark very short events for manual review)
